newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Bank DKI cuts bond coupon to 15.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Bank DKI cuts bond coupon to 15.0 pct.

text.p: Indonesia's Bank DKI, owned by the Jakarta local government, had reduced the coupon for its seven-year 500 billion rupiah bonds due to over-subscription, a bank official said.
An official at Bank DKI told Reuters that the initially fixed coupons of 15.5 percent for the first six months were cut to 15.0 percent.
She said the subsequent coupons remained unchanged, based on the six-month deposit rates of five state-owned banks plus a premium of one percentage point.
The bonds, attached with coupons payable every quarter, were well received despite the rate cut, an official with lead underwriter PT Sucorinvest Central Gani said.
But both officials declined to give details of the percentage of oversubscription.
The bank official said 43 underwriters were participating in the straight bonds issue. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
